work.name: anthill.txt
work.title: anthill ai, founding research engineer
body: # anthill ai
founding research engineer. small team, so the job is wide.
- retrieval for llms: chunking, hybrid search, rerankers, and the evals that tell you which of those actually mattered.
- knowledge graphs: pulling entities and relations out of messy enterprise docs and letting agents walk them.
- agents: tool-using loops that can be trusted to stop. most of the work is in the stopping.
- text-to-sql: natural language over real warehouses, where the schema has 400 tables and three of them are named `orders`.
stack: python, typescript, google cloud, postgres, more sql than i expected.

projects.name: bi-gan.md
projects.title: bi-gan for lattice structures
body: # bi-gan for lattice structure identification
final year project at iit jodhpur.
trained a bidirectional gan to map between lattice structure images and a latent space, then used the encoder half for identification. the generator was the bait; the encoder was the point.
later i reused the same architecture for portfolio stress testing: encode market regimes, sample from the latent space, decode plausible-but-unseen scenarios. same model, different physics.
what i took from it: a model trained on crystal lattices will happily hallucinate a market crash. most ideas transfer if you squint.

projects.name: text-to-sql.md
projects.title: text-to-sql, in production
body: # text-to-sql
the thing i spend most of my week on. notes, not a writeup.
- schema linking matters more than the model. find the right three tables and a small model does fine.
- generate, execute, repair. the repair loop is where the accuracy lives.
- evals on real questions from real users beat spider and bird. people ask weirder things.

lab.name: less-data.md
lab.title: learning from less
body: # learning from less
the question i keep coming back to: how could machines learn more like brains do, from less data and with less compute?
- a child sees maybe a few thousand cats. a vision model sees millions and still gets fooled by a sticker.
- current bets: better priors, active sampling, and memory that is not just a bigger context window.
this is a lab file. it is allowed to be wrong.

lab.name: blip.md
lab.title: blip
body: # blip
the robot wandering around this page. 12x12 pixels, two walk frames, one blink, one hop.
- steering is three rules: wander, avoid the text column, go to the nearest bit.
- it looks at your cursor because every pet should.
- try: `blip --count 4`, `drop`, `kill blip`, `rm -rf /`.

lab.name: this-site.md
lab.title: this site
body: # this site
vite, vanilla typescript, one json file for content, no framework.
- the terminal has a parser, a fake filesystem and a command registry. adding a command is one object.
- the sprite engine is a requestanimationframe loop and some vectors.
- under 80kb of js. no gradients were harmed.
[source on github](https://github.com/nsquaredzz/nsquaredzz.github.io)
